books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Constitution of the State of California, Article I, Section 18 (1849)

stimulus.source_note: Constitution of the State of California, Article I, Section 18, adopted at Monterey, 1849. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
Neither slavery, nor involuntary servitude, unless for the punishment of crimes, shall ever be tolerated in this State.

[Original summary: California's convention wrote this constitution at Monterey in the fall of 1849, after gold drew tens of thousands of settlers to the territory in a single year. The convention asked Congress to admit California as a free state.]

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: According to Article I, Section 18, slavery could be tolerated in California only

options.text: in the gold mines, where labor was scarce.
options.misconception: Gold mines appear nowhere in the section; the only exception is punishment for crimes.

options.text: on land owned by Californians before 1849.
options.misconception: The section names no exception for earlier landowners; its only exception is punishment for crimes.

options.text: until Congress voted to admit California.
options.misconception: The section bans slavery in the state itself; it does not make the ban wait for Congress.

rationales.A: Gold mines appear nowhere in the section; the only exception is punishment for crimes.
rationales.B: The section bans slavery outright, “unless for the punishment of crimes” — punishment is the only exception it names.
rationales.C: The section names no exception for earlier landowners; its only exception is punishment for crimes.
rationales.D: The section bans slavery in the state itself; it does not make the ban wait for Congress.
rationales.general:
1. Read the ban as Californians wrote it: neither slavery nor involuntary servitude shall ever be tolerated.
2. Find the single crack in that wall: “unless for the punishment of crimes.”
3. Test each answer against that crack: only punishment for a crime fits through it.
Remember: in a legal ban, the exception clause is the whole answer — read it before the ban itself.
